The World Health Organization (WHO) has urged scientists to destroy samples of a deadly flu virus that could trigger a global pandemic. The virus, known as A/H2N2, was first detected by a Canadian laboratory, which reported the finding to the Public Health Agency of Canada on March 26. That agency then notified the WHO and other national health authorities. The WHO confirmed that 10 countries have already destroyed their samples, and five others are in the process of doing so.

However, shipments of the virus sent to Mexico and Lebanon remain unaccounted for. Meridian Bioscience had distributed routine testing kits contaminated with the virus to nearly 5,000 laboratories worldwide. So far, 3,747 of these labs—mostly in North America—have been identified as having received the material.

A/H2N2 is a variant of the strain responsible for the 1957 Asian Flu Pandemic. It was later replaced by the H3N2 variant. Since people born after 1959 did not encounter this version during childhood, they are unlikely to have immunity. The WHO continues to monitor the situation, stressing the importance of containment and proper handling of any remaining samples.

Non-traumatic headaches accounted for 2.3% of 10,450 emergency department (ED) admissions, with 77.8% of patients female. Headache etiology was classified as primary (59.4%), non-primary (secondary headaches and neuralgias, 32%), or unclassified (8.6%). Migraine was the most common primary headache, while cervical myofascial pain was the most frequent non-primary cause.

All patients presenting with headache at the ED triage were assessed using the International Headache Classification, third edition (ICHID 3) criteria. Those meeting ICHD 3 criteria for primary headache were managed per standard care and followed up by phone within 48 hours to confirm resolution. Patients not meeting ICHD 3 criteria for primary headache were admitted for further diagnostic evaluation and management.

The proportion of patients fulfilling ICHD 3 criteria was significantly higher in those with primary headaches (OR: 18.7, 95% CI 7.1–48.6). A history of migraine (OR: 2.9, 95% CI 2.1–3.9) and a history of similar headache episodes (OR: 2.7, 95% CI 2.3–3.3) were independently associated with primary headache diagnoses. Non-primary etiologies were significantly linked to immunosuppression (OR: 2.7, 95% CI 2.3–3.3) and age over 50 (OR: 2.7, 95% CI 2.01–3.62). Abnormal neurological exam, sudden onset, and sleep-related headache onset were not statistically significant predictors of non-primary etiology.

Red flag features—age at presentation, sleep onset, associated symptoms, abnormal neurological exam, sudden onset, nonresponse to analgesics, and prior consultation—were evaluated across groups. The presence of ICHD 3 criteria, history of migraine, and prior similar episodes were strongly linked to primary headache classification.

These findings indicate that adherence to ICHD 3 criteria enhances differentiation between primary and non-primary headaches in the ED setting. The diagnostic utility of ICHD 3 criteria, immunosuppression, age over 50, history of migraine, and recurrent headache patterns supports their use in clinical decision-making to guide appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic pathways.

The United Nations (UN) faces serious allegations of corruption and misconduct, including bribery, sexual misconduct, and involvement in the Iraq's Oil-for-Food program. These allegations, if proven, could severely damage the organization's credibility and even threaten its existence. Among the most severe accusations are those involving the Oil-for-Food program, which was established in 1996 to allow Iraq to sell oil in exchange for food, medicine, and other humanitarian supplies. The program was intended to help the Iraqi government meet the basic needs of its citizens, who were suffering under international economic sanctions imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in 1990. The sanctions were designed to prevent Iraq from rebuilding its military forces.

The Oil-for-Food program began in October 1997, with the first deliveries arriving in March 1998. It used a trustee deposit system, where the money from oil sales was paid into an account inaccessible to the Iraqi government. A portion of these funds was used to pay for damages caused to Kuwait and to help cover the costs of coalition forces and other UN expenses related to Iraq. The remaining money stayed in the account, and the Iraqi government could use it to purchase non-prohibited items.

However, serious allegations of corruption, fraud, and collusion with former dictator Saddam Hussein have surfaced against UN staff, companies, and politicians from several countries. Even UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan has faced suspicions of involvement in the corruption scheme, as has his son, Kojo Annan. The gravity of these allegations threatens not only the credibility of the UN but also its very existence.

In response to these allegations, Secretary-General Kofi Annan has announced plans to promote reforms within the organization. The Oil-for-Food program was intended to provide humanitarian aid to the Iraqi people, with approximately 60% of Iraq's 26 million inhabitants relying solely on the program's food rations. Around $27 billion worth of humanitarian supplies were delivered to Iraq through the program.

The program's approval process for purchases was complex. Certain items, such as food, were prioritized and delivered quickly. Most items, including simple goods like pencils and folic acid, required extensive review, typically taking about six months before approval. Items considered dual-use, meaning they could potentially be used for biological, chemical, or nuclear weapons, as well as those with long delivery times, were rejected, regardless of the justification provided by the Iraqi government.

Non-traumatic headaches account for 0.5 to 4.5% at the emergency department (ED). Although primary headaches represent the most common causes, the likelihood of ominous etiology has to be considered by clinicians in order to avoid diagnostic and therapeutic pitfalls. Due to the absence of biological or imaging findings to diagnose primary headaches we hypothesize ICHD 3(International Headache criteria 3) criteria as a useful tool at the moment to identify and to establish a difference between those patients who are undergoing primary headaches and those who will need advanced diagnostic strategies.

To determine the usefulness of ICHD 3 criteria to differentiate primary from non-primary headaches at the emergency department (ED).

During five weeks all the patients complaining of headache attended at the triage unit at the ED were interviewed, examined and classified as having primary or non-primary headaches by means of ICHD 3 criteria. Those patients with primary headaches were treated according to standard of care protocols and followed up by means of phone call communication after 48 hours to assure satisfactory outcome. Those patients classified as having non-primary headaches (secondary headaches and neuralgias) were admitted for additional diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Between both groups we compared the prevalence of fulfilled criteria for primary headaches and the proportion of traditional red flags such as age, sleep headache onset, associated symptoms, abnormal neurological exam, sudden onset, and nonresponse to analgesics in addition to previous consultation before this evaluation.

Headache was responsible for 244 (2.3%) out of 10450 admissions at the ED, 77.8% were females. Primary, non-primary (secondary plus neuralgias) and unclassified headaches were 59.4%, 32% and 8.6% respectively. Migraine and cervical myofascial pain were the most frequent etiologies for primary and non-primary causes respectively. Factors associated to non-primary etiologies were immunosuppression (OR: 2.7 IC 95% 2.3–3.3) and age older than 50 (OR: 2.7 IC 95% 2.01–3.62). Abnormal neurological exam, sudden and sleep headache onset were not statistically significant.

Factors found to be associated with primary headaches were: fulfilling ICHD 3 criteria (OR: 18.7, IC95% 7.1–48.6), history of migraine (OR: 2.9 IC 95% 2.1–3.9), and history of similar episodes (OR: 2.7 IC 95% 2.3–3.3).

This data suggests that fulfilling ICHD 3 criteria could be useful to differentiate primary from non-primary headaches. This observation is also valid for immunosuppression, age older than 50, history of migraine and history of similar episodes.
</source>

text:
The development of high-yielding rice varieties with drought tolerance is essential for the sustainable livelihoods of farmers in rainfed rice ecosystems. Genomic selection (GS) offers a promising approach for breeding such complex traits. We assessed the efficacy of two novel implementations of GS: trait- and environment-specific marker selection and the application of multi-environment prediction models. A reference population of 280 rainfed lowland accessions, genotyped with 215k SNP markers, was phenotyped under favorable and two managed drought environments. For each trait and environment, trait-specific SNP subsets (28k) were selected using genome-wide association study (GWAS) results from the complete genotype dataset.

We compared the performance of single-environment and multi-environment genomic prediction models using kernel regression methods (GBLUP and RKHS) under two cross-validation scenarios: CV1 (no phenotypic data for the validation set in one environment) and CV2 (phenotypic data available for the validation set in one environment). Trait-specific marker selection enhanced the predictive ability (PA) of genomic predictions by up to 22% compared to markers selected based on neutral linkage disequilibrium (LD). Multi-environment models, particularly those based on RKHS, improved drought stress tolerance predictions by up to 32% under the CV2 strategy. However, under the less favorable CV1 strategy, multi-environment models achieved similar PA to single-environment predictions.

Additionally, we found that reasonable predictive ability could be attained with as few as 3,000 SNP markers, even in populations with low LD, when marker selection is based on pairwise LD. These findings have significant implications for breeding programs focused on drought tolerance. The most resource-efficient strategy would involve accurate phenotyping of the reference population under both favorable and managed drought conditions, while the candidate population would only need phenotyping in one of these environments.

Developing high yielding rice varieties that are tolerant to drought stress is crucial for the sustainable livelihood of rice farmers in rainfed rice cropping ecosystems. Genomic selection (GS) promises to be an effective breeding option for these complex traits. We evaluated the effectiveness of two rather new options in the implementation of GS: trait and environment-specific marker selection and the use of multi-environment prediction models. Under the less favorable CV1 strategy, the multi-environment models achieved similar PA than the single-environment predictions. We also showed that reasonable PA could be obtained with as few as 3,000 SNP markers, even in a population of low LD extent, provided marker selection is based on pairwise LD. The implications of these findings for breeding for drought tolerance are discussed. text: In everyday life, people frequently combine emotion regulation strategies. Yet most research has treated these strategies as if they operate independently. The current study examines how reappraisal and rumination interact when used in sequence to influence anger. Participants (N = 156) first recalled a recent anger-provoking event, then followed one of four instructions: (a) reappraise twice, (b) reappraise first, then ruminate, (c) ruminate first, then reappraise, or (d) ruminate twice. As in prior research, reappraisal alone reduced anger, while rumination alone showed no significant effect. However, a small interaction emerged: those who ruminated first and then reappraised reported a greater reduction in anger than those who reappraised first and then ruminated. No other differences emerged between groups. These findings suggest that the second strategy does exert an effect beyond the first, but this effect is modest. Thus, while the order of strategy use matters, the initial choice of strategy—particularly whether it is reappraisal—appears to carry the most weight in shaping the emotional experience. The results underscore the importance of considering strategy sequence, even if the overall impact remains limited.

The Associated Press (AP) and CNN reported midday UTC that the death toll from Sunday’s accident on K2 has risen to eleven.

Two Dutch climbers were rescued by helicopter, according to the AP. CNN reported that two of the dead were attempting to assist others while ascending the mountain.

AP said about two dozen climbers began their ascent of K2— the world’s second-highest peak— on Friday, after weather conditions improved. The climbers were from the Netherlands, South Korea, Italy, Norway, France, Nepal, Serbia, Pakistan, and Ireland.

Trouble started Sunday when several climbers decided to turn back due to issues with rope placement. CNN reported the group was split into two teams, both descending from near the summit when a large chunk of ice broke loose and swept three people from the mountain.

Wilco Van Rooijen, one of the two rescued Dutch climbers, spoke to AP by phone. He cited poor planning in addition to the avalanche as contributing factors. He said a low-cloud bank caused a whiteout, but he chose to begin descending from near the summit.

One stranded climber, Marco Confortola of Italy, reached his brother by phone and described the events as hellish. A helicopter rescue for Confortola was delayed by poor weather, but he eventually made it to base camp on foot.

CNN reported this is the deadliest accident on K2 since records began in 1939. Since then, 66 people—not including those in this incident—have died on the mountain.

text:
Lung cancer is the most prevalent adult malignancy and the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Iron (Fe) is an essential trace element integral to multiple metabolic pathways and critical physiological functions. This case-control study investigated the association between serum iron concentration, iron metabolism parameters, and genetic variation in seven genes involved in iron homeostasis and antioxidant defense—HFE, TFR1, HAMP, TF, SOD2, CAT, and GPX1—with lung cancer incidence in a Polish cohort.

The study included 200 lung cancer patients and 200 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Serum iron, total iron-binding capacity (TIBC), unsaturated iron-binding capacity (UIBC), serum ferritin, and transferrin saturation were measured. Seven single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were genotyped across the targeted genes.

Lung cancer patients exhibited significantly higher mean serum iron (p = 0.01), ferritin (p = 0.007), and TIBC (p = 0.006) compared to controls. Individuals in the highest quartile (IVth) of serum iron and ferritin had more than twofold increased risk of lung cancer relative to those in the lowest quartile (Ist). Higher transferrin saturation (p = 0.01) and lower TIBC (p < 0.01) were associated with improved survival outcomes in lung cancer patients. No significant differences in genotype distribution were observed between cases and controls for most variants. However, the rs10421768 polymorphism in HAMP showed a borderline significant association with increased lung cancer risk (OR = 2.83, p = 0.05).

These findings suggest that elevated systemic iron levels, as indicated by serum iron and ferritin, may contribute to lung cancer incidence. The rs10421768 variant in HAMP may confer approximately threefold increased risk. Paradoxically, higher iron burden may also be linked to better survival in established lung cancer, warranting further investigation into iron’s dual role in carcinogenesis and disease progression.

Allegations of corruption, bribery, and sexual misconduct involving United Nations (UN) peacekeepers have put the organization's credibility at risk.

Among the most serious allegations are those surrounding the UN's Oil-for-Food program in Iraq. Accusations of bribery, fraudulent accounting, and collusion with former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein have been leveled against UN staff, private companies, and politicians from several countries. Even UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan has faced suspicion regarding his alleged involvement in the corruption scheme, as have his son, Kojo Annan.

These allegations pose a significant threat, not just to the UN's credibility, but to its very existence.

In response to these allegations, Secretary-General Kofi Annan has announced plans to implement reforms within the organization.

The Oil-for-Food Program was established by the UN in 1996. It allowed Iraq to sell oil on the world market in exchange for food, medicine, and other humanitarian supplies. The program's stated goal was to help the Iraqi government meet the basic needs of its citizens, who were suffering under international economic sanctions imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990. The sanctions were designed to prevent Iraq from rebuilding its military forces.

Iraq initially rejected the program but later signed a memorandum in May 1996 for its implementation. The program began in October 1997, with the first deliveries arriving in March 1998.

The program used a trust fund system, whereby the money from Iraq's oil sales was paid into an account inaccessible to the Iraqi government. A portion of these funds was used to pay reparations for damages caused to Kuwait, and another portion helped cover the expenses of coalition forces and other UN costs related to Iraq. The remaining money stayed in the account.

The Iraqi government was permitted to purchase non-prohibited items using these funds. Certain items, such as food, were prioritized, and the corresponding goods were delivered immediately. Most items, including seemingly innocuous products like pencils and folic acid, required approval, a process that typically took around six months. Items deemed to have potential use in biological, chemical, or nuclear weapons, as well as those with long delivery times, were denied, regardless of the justification provided for their request.

Approximately 60 percent of Iraq's 26 million inhabitants relied solely on the Oil-for-Food Program's provisions for survival. Humanitarian aid valued at around $27 billion was delivered to Iraq through this program.

There are many types of disabilities, each associated with distinct socioeconomic factors that influence health outcomes. However, nationally representative surveys on the oral health status of disabled populations in Korea remain limited.

For the DMFT index, MD individuals showed an odds ratio of 1.34 (95% CI, 1.03–1.74), and those with multiple disabilities, 1.75 (95% CI, 1.11–2.76).

These findings confirm a substantially poorer oral health status among disabled individuals compared to non-disabled peers. The results demonstrate that both the presence and type of disability significantly influence oral health outcomes. This distinction is critical for accurately assessing the needs of disabled populations and informing targeted public health interventions.

Rab proteins are key players in managing the ins and outs of cellular dynamics, and they've been found to be quite the multitaskers when it comes to leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2). This enzyme is a bit of a big deal in Parkinson’s disease (PD), as it's linked to both inherited and sporadic cases. Rabs not only help LRRK2 do its job but also get a little something back in the form of phosphorylation. Some of these Rabs, like Rab32, Rab38, and Rab29, have been caught hanging out with LRRK2, even helping it find its way around the cell. For instance, Rab29 acts as a tour guide, leading LRRK2 to the Golgi and getting Rab8 and Rab10 all fired up with phosphorylation.

Rab32, in particular, is a bit of a jack-of-all-trades, involved in everything from endosomal trafficking to mitochondrial dynamics and even melanosome biogenesis. And get this, a little tweak in Rab32 has been tied to PD too. Now, here's where things get interesting. We've found that Rab32 and sorting nexin 6 (SNX6) are quite the pair, interacting directly with each other. SNX6 is like a temporary member of the retromer team, which is a complex that shuttles stuff back from the endosomes to the Golgi. And would you believe, the retromer's Vps35 subunit is also linked to PD? It doesn't stop there. Both Rab32 and SNX6 seem to have a hand in where cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptors end up, which are usually sent back to the trans-Golgi network (TGN) by the retromer. So, it looks like Rab32 is playing a role in SNX6/retromer trafficking at the Golgi. And here's the kicker, this might just hint at a connection between the retromer and Rab32 in LRRK2's travels and functions.

The Rab family of small GTPases regulate various aspects of cellular dynamics in eukaryotic cells. Membrane trafficking has emerged as central to the functions of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2), which is associated with inherited and sporadic forms of Parkinson’s disease (PD). Rabs act as both regulators of the catalytic activity and targets for serine/threonine phosphorylation by LRRK2. Rab32, Rab38 and Rab29 have been shown to regulate LRRK2 sub-cellular localization through direct interactions. Recently, Rab29 was shown to escort LRRK2 to the Golgi apparatus and activate the phosphorylation of Rab8 and Rab10. Rab32 is linked to multiple cellular functions including endosomal trafficking, mitochondrial dynamics, and melanosome biogenesis. A missense mutation in Rab32 has also recently been linked to PD. Here, we demonstrate that Rab32 directly interacts with sorting nexin 6 (SNX6). SNX6 is a transient subunit of the retromer, an endosome-Golgi retrieval complex whose Vps35 subunit is strongly associated with PD. We could further show that localization of cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptors, which are recycled to the trans-Golgi network (TGN) by the retromer, was affected by both Rab32 and SNX6. These data imply that Rab32 is linked to SNX6/retromer trafficking at the Golgi, and also suggests a possible connection between the retromer and Rab32 in the trafficking and biological functions of LRRK2.

text: This study investigates the epidemiological and spatial patterns of domestic and community interpersonal violence using three years of violent trauma data from Campina Grande, a medium-sized city in North-Eastern Brazil. A total of 3559 medical and police records were analyzed, with 2563 cases included in the final assessment to examine socioeconomic and geographic factors. Logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between sociodemographic, temporal, and incident characteristics and domestic violence. Geographical Information Systems (GIS) were employed to map victims’ household addresses and identify spatial clusters. Female individuals, those who were divorced, or living with a partner were more likely to experience domestic violence when the perpetrator was male. The use of firearms in domestic violence incidents was rare. Eight out of ten domestic violence victims were women, and the female-to-male ratio was 3.3 times higher than in community violence cases. Unmarried cohabiting couples were twice as likely to experience a domestic violence incident within the family unit (OR = 2.03) compared to married couples. Seven geographical hotspots were identified, with the highest density concentrated in the eastern part of the study area, which also had the lowest average household income. Aggressor sex, marital status, and mechanism of injury were strongly associated with domestic violence. Low-income neighborhoods were linked to both domestic and non-domestic violence hotspots, suggesting a spatial overlap between economic disadvantage and interpersonal violence. These findings support the view that economic poverty may be a significant factor in the occurrence of interpersonal violence, particularly within the domestic sphere.

About 90 officers from multiple agencies dispersed a gathering described as a rave in the Diamond Fork area of Spanish Fork Canyon, roughly an hour’s drive from Salt Lake City, Utah, around 11:30 p.m. Saturday (5:30 a.m. Sunday UTC). The event took place across both public and private land, prompting a coordinated response.

Utah County Sheriff’s Office officials said they had been probing similar events since the start of the season. In a press release, the department cited prior allegations of sexual abuse at other raves, along with separate incidents involving firearms and theft, as grounds for the investigation. The release also noted that no valid mass gathering permit had been secured for this event. Promoters dispute this, asserting they obtained all necessary permits legally and have provided a permit number: #2005-11.

State officials clarify that while a permit from the Utah County Health Department's Bureau of Environmental Health Services was issued—confirmed by Jay Stone, the department’s mass gathering permit coordinator—a separate Utah State mass gathering permit was also required. The promoters maintain they held the correct authorization.

Authorities reported that more than 60 people were arrested, primarily for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, underage drinking, drug possession and distribution, resisting arrest, assault on an officer, disorderly conduct, and one weapons-related offense: a pistol found in a private residence on the event property. Confiscated items included cocaine, ecstasy, marijuana, hallucinogenic mushrooms, alcohol, and drug paraphernalia. Some of the drugs may have been seized by private security personnel, who were also arrested.

Eyewitnesses, including several attendees, reported that the police response involved excessive force—describing beatings, taserings, and attacks by police dogs. Sheriff Jim Tracy acknowledged that dogs and tasers were present during the operation but stated that tasers were not deployed on anyone and that no dogs were used against the crowd. 

Sergeant Darren Gilbert of the Utah County Sheriff’s Office also reported that a 17-year-old girl was found unconscious and later treated for an ecstasy overdose, then released to her parents. An advertisement for the event listed an attorney as being on site. The local sheriff is scheduled to appear on a Utah television news program.

text: Prolonged use of numerous clinically available drugs is associated with disturbances in glucose homeostasis, a recognized pathway to the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study investigates the potential for drug-induced disruption of glucose regulation through off-target interactions with gut hormone receptors, including glucagon receptor (GCGR), glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R), and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR). These receptors, primarily expressed in the gastrointestinal tract, play a critical role in modulating insulin secretion, glucagon release, and food intake. While incretin-based therapies targeting GLP1R and GIPR have gained clinical prominence due to their glucose-lowering efficacy and favorable metabolic profile, recent advances in the structural characterization of GLP1R have enabled a deeper evaluation of pharmacological targeting opportunities. Using an in silico approach, we analyzed a broad set of well-established pharmaceutical agents for their potential to bind to these gut hormone receptors as unintended targets. Our analysis revealed that compounds exhibiting the highest binding affinity for GLP1R and GIPR were frequently reported in pharmacovigilance databases as having minimal impact on glucose metabolism within their respective therapeutic classes. This observation suggests that strong binding to these receptors may result in functional modulation—potentially through stimulation of GLP1R and GIPR, or inhibition of GCGR—leading to enhanced insulin secretion and reduced hepatic glucose output. Such effects may counteract the glucose-intolerant side effects commonly observed with other drug classes, thereby offering a protective metabolic effect that mitigates the risk of drug-induced T2DM. Furthermore, the screen identified several top-scoring molecules from the ZINC15 database that demonstrate high-affinity binding to the gut hormone receptor structures, positioning them as promising non-peptidic candidates for repositioning as alternative therapeutics to existing incretin mimetics. These findings underscore the significance of receptor-level off-target profiling in drug development and suggest that compounds with high binding potential to gut hormone receptors may represent both a risk mitigation strategy and a novel pathway for therapeutic innovation.

text: In daily emotional experience, people frequently combine multiple emotion regulation strategies, yet most research has examined them in isolation. This study investigates how the sequence of reappraisal and rumination influences anger, focusing on their interactive effects. One hundred fifty-six participants recalled a recent anger-provoking event and were randomly assigned to one of four conditions: (a) two reappraisal attempts, (b) reappraisal followed by rumination, (c) rumination followed by reappraisal, or (d) two rumination attempts. As expected, reappraisal alone led to a reduction in anger, consistent with prior findings. Rumination, in contrast, was associated with no significant change in anger levels. The key finding was a small but significant interaction: participants who ruminated first and then reappraised reported greater reductions in anger than those who used reappraisal first and then ruminated. No other differences emerged between conditions. These results suggest that while the first strategy used has a dominant influence, the second strategy still exerts a modest effect beyond the initial one. The order of strategy use, particularly placing reappraisal after rumination, may modestly enhance anger reduction, though the effect size remains small. These findings underscore that strategy sequences matter, even if their impact is limited, and highlight the need to consider temporal dynamics in emotion regulation research.

Voltage-sensing phosphatases (VSPs) are transmembrane proteins that link changes in membrane potential to the hydrolysis of inositol signaling lipids. These enzymes dephosphorylate phosphatidylinositol phosphates (PIPs), which regulate various aspects of cell membrane physiology, including cell division, growth, and migration. VSPs are highly conserved among chordates, with their RNA transcripts detected in both adult and embryonic stages across various species, such as frogs, fish, chickens, mice, and humans. Using reverse transcriptase-PCR (RT-PCR), we demonstrated that both Xenopus laevis VSPs (Xl-VSP1 and Xl-VSP2) mRNAs are expressed in early embryos, implying their involvement in early tadpole development. Western blot analysis with a VSP antibody revealed increasing levels of Xl-VSP protein during embryonic development. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) showed that Xl-VSP protein is specifically localized to the apical membrane of both embryonic and adult kidney tubules.

Furthermore, we characterized the catalytic activity of both Xl-VSP homologs. Xl-VSP1 catalyzes the removal of 3- and 5-phosphates, whereas Xl-VSP2 is a less efficient 3-phosphatase with distinct substrate specificity. These findings suggest that Xl-VSP1 and Xl-VSP2 have different functional roles and that VSPs are integral components of voltage-dependent PIP signaling pathways during vertebrate kidney tubule development and function.

Right now, the projected majority for opposition parties FDP and CDU is getting smaller, while the current government parties Greens, SPD, and the Left Party are gaining ground.

text:
There are many types of disabilities, and each type has a variety related to socioeconomic factors. Such factors affect to many health problems of the disabled. However, surveys of the oral health status of the disabled in Korea are rare.

The purpose of this study was to estimate oral health disparity through comparing oral health status of the disabled to the non-disabled, adjusted for the net effect of the disability on oral health status.

A cross-sectional study was conducted among the disabled in urban and suburban areas in Korea from June to September 2016. People with physical, mental, and multiple disabilities took part in this survey. The clinical examinations were carried out by trained dentists. Statistical analysis was performed to quantify the association between oral health and socioeconomic status after restricting the analysis using a propensity score matching method.

The disabled had more DMFT, DT, and MT, fewer FT, and fewer teeth than the non-disabled based on entire groups (P<0.01). No difference in the ratio of periodontitis was observed. The subjects with mental disabilities (MD) scored 3.09 (95% CI, 1.07–8.97), and those with multiple disabilities scored 4.37 (95% CI, 1.16–16.37) for edentulous status. The MD had an odds ratio of 1.34 (95% CI, 1.03–1.74), and those with multiple disabilities had an odds ratio of 1.75 (95% CI, 1.11–2.76) for the DMFT index.

These results represent poor oral health status of the disabled compared to the non-disabled. Consequentially, we can verify that not only the existence of disability but also the type of disability has a decisive effect on oral health condition. This comparison is necessary to widen our approach to evaluate the actual status condition of the disabled.

text: This study explores both epidemiological and spatial characteristics of domestic and community interpersonal violence. We evaluated three years of violent trauma data in the medium-sized city of Campina Grande in North-Eastern Brazil. 3559 medical and police records were analysed and 2563 cases were included to identify socioeconomic and geographic patterns. The associations between sociodemographic, temporal, and incident characteristics and domestic violence were evaluated using logistic regression. Using Geographical Information Systems (GIS), we mapped victims’ household addresses to identify spatial patterns. We observed a higher incidence of domestic violence among female, divorced, or co-habitant persons when the violent event was perpetrated by males. There was only a minor chance of occurrence of domestic violence involving firearms. 8 out of 10 victims of domestic violence were women and the female/male ratio was 3.3 times greater than that of community violence (violence not occurring in the home). Unmarried couples were twice as likely to have a victim in the family unit (OR = 2.03), compared to married couples. Seven geographical hotspots were identified. The greatest density of hotspots was found in the East side of the study area and was spatially coincident with the lowest average family income. Aggressor sex, marital status, and mechanism of injury were most associated with domestic violence, and low-income neighbourhoods were coincident with both domestic and non-domestic violence hotspots. These results provide further evidence that economic poverty may play a significant role in interpersonal, and particularly domestic violence.

text: Finding safe and effective treatments for chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in the elderly is of clinical interest given the comorbidities and associated polypharmacy in this population. However, the number of patients older than age 65 years enrolled into clinical trials of anti-HCV medications generally have been limited and thus reaching meaningful conclusions for this demographic has been difficult. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is a once-daily, all-oral, ribavirin-free, pangenotypic direct-acting antiviral (DAA) combination therapy that has demonstrated high sustained virologic response rates at post-treatment week 12 (SVR12) and a favorable safety profile in patients with chronic HCV infection. This analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir in patients aged ≥65 years. Data were pooled for treatment-naïve and -experienced patients with chronic HCV genotype (GT) 1–6 infections who received glecaprevir/pibrentasvir for 8, 12, or 16 weeks in 9 Phase 2 and 3 trials. SVR12 and adverse events (AEs) were evaluated for patients aged ≥65 versus <65 years. Of the 2369 patients enrolled, 328 (14%) were aged ≥65 years. Among patients aged ≥65 years, 42% and 34% had GT1 and GT2, respectively; 40% were treatment-experienced and 20% had compensated cirrhosis. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir treatment resulted in SVR12 rates of 97.9% (95% CI, 96.3–99.4; n/N = 321/328) for patients aged ≥65 years and 97.3% (95% CI, 96.6–98.0; n/N = 1986/2041) for patients aged <65 years. The rates were not significantly different between the two age groups (P = 0.555). DAA-related AEs leading to treatment discontinuation, or serious AEs were similarly rare (<0.5%) for patients ≥65 and <65 years old. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is an efficacious and well-tolerated treatment option for patients aged ≥65 years with chronic HCV infection.

Lung cancer is the most common adult malignancy accounting for the largest proportion of cancer related deaths. Iron (Fe) is an essential trace element and is a component of several major metabolic pathways playing an important role in many physiological processes. In this study we evaluated the association between Fe concentration in serum, iron metabolism parameters and genetic variaton in 7 genes involved in iron metabolism and anti-oxidative processes with the incidence of lung cancer in Poland.

The study included 200 lung cancer patients and 200 matched healthy control subjects. We analyzed serum iron concentration and iron metabolism parameters (TIBC, UIBC, serum ferritin and transferrin saturation), and genotyped seven variants in seven genes: HFE, TFR1, HAMP, TF, SOD2, CAT and GPX1.

Lung cancer patients compared to their matched controls had significantly higher mean serum iron level (p = 0.01), ferritin level (p = 0.007) and TIBC (p = 0.006). Analysis revealed that higher concentration of iron and ferritin (IVth quartile) compared to the lower concentration (Ist quartile) was associated with over 2-fold increased lung cancer incidence. We also found that higher transferrin saturation (p = 0.01) and lower TIBC (p<0.01) are associated with better survival of lung cancer patients. The analysis of polymorphisms in iron related genes did not reveal a significant difference between lung cancer patients and controls. However, rs10421768 in HAMP showed a borderline statistically significant correlation with lung cancer risk (OR = 2.83, p = 0.05).

The results of this case control study indicate that higher body iron represented by higher Fe and ferritin levels may be associated with lung cancer incidence. Rs10421768 in HAMP may be associated with about 3-times higher lung cancer risk. Higher Fe body content may be associated with better survival of lung cancer patients.

text: We developed a novel skin regeneration therapy combining nevus tissue inactivated by high hydrostatic pressure (HHP) in the reconstruction of the dermis with a cultured epidermal autograft (CEA). The issue with this treatment is the unstable survival of CEA on the inactivated dermis. In this study, we applied collagen/gelatin sponge (CGS), which can sustain the release of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF), to the inactivated skin in order to accelerate angiogenesis. Murine skin grafts from C57BL6J/Jcl mice (8 mm in diameter) were prepared, inactivated by HHP and cryopreserved. One month later, the grafts were transplanted subcutaneously onto the back of other mice and covered by CGS impregnated with saline or bFGF. Grafts were harvested after one, two and eight weeks, at which point the engraftment was evaluated through the histology and angiogenesis-related gene expressions were determined by real-time polymerase chain reaction. Histological sections showed that the dermal cellular density and newly formed capillaries in the bFGF group were significantly higher than in the control group. The relative expression of FGF-2, PDGF-A and VEGF-A genes in the bFGF group was significantly higher than in the control group at Week 1. This study suggested that the angiogenesis into grafts was accelerated, which might improve the engraftment of inactivated dermis in combination with the sustained release of bFGF by CGSs.

text:
Non-traumatic headaches account for 0.5 to 4.5% at the emergency department (ED). Although primary headaches represent the most common causes, the likelihood of ominous etiology has to be considered by clinicians in order to avoid diagnostic and therapeutic pitfalls. Due to the absence of biological or imaging findings to diagnose primary headaches we hypothesize ICHD 3(International Headache criteria 3) criteria as a useful tool at the moment to identify and to establish a difference between those patients who are undergoing primary headaches and those who will need advanced diagnostic strategies.

To determine the usefulness of ICHD 3 criteria to differentiate primary from non-primary headaches at the emergency department (ED).

During five weeks all the patients complaining of headache attended at the triage unit at the ED were interviewed, examined and classified as having primary or non-primary headaches by means of ICHD 3 criteria. Those patients with primary headaches were treated according to standard of care protocols and followed up by means of phone call communication after 48 hours to assure satisfactory outcome. Those patients classified as having non-primary headaches (secondary headaches and neuralgias) were admitted for additional diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Between both groups we compared the prevalence of fulfilled criteria for primary headaches and the proportion of traditional red flags such as age, sleep headache onset, associated symptoms, abnormal neurological exam, sudden onset, and nonresponse to analgesics in addition to previous consultation before this evaluation.

Headache was responsible for 244 (2.3%) out of 10450 admissions at the ED, 77.8% were females. Primary, non-primary (secondary plus neuralgias) and unclassified headaches were 59.4%, 32% and 8.6% respectively. Migraine and cervical myofascial pain were the most frequent etiologies for primary and non-primary causes respectively. Factors associated to non-primary etiologies were immunosuppression (OR: 2.7 IC 95% 2.3–3.3) and age older than 50 (OR: 2.7 IC 95% 2.01–3.62). Abnormal neurological exam, sudden and sleep headache onset were not statistically significant.

Factors found to be associated with primary headaches were: fulfilling ICHD 3 criteria (OR: 18.7, IC95% 7.1–48.6), history of migraine (OR: 2.9 IC 95% 2.1–3.9), and history of similar episodes (OR: 2.7 IC 95% 2.3–3.3).

This data suggests that fulfilling ICHD 3 criteria could be useful to differentiate primary from non-primary headaches. This observation is also valid for immunosuppression, age older than 50, history of migraine and history of similar episodes.

text: Developing high yielding rice varieties that are tolerant to drought stress is crucial for the sustainable livelihood of rice farmers in rainfed rice cropping ecosystems. Genomic selection (GS) promises to be an effective breeding option for these complex traits. We evaluated the effectiveness of two rather new options in the implementation of GS: trait and environment-specific marker selection and the use of multi-environment prediction models. A reference population of 280 rainfed lowland accessions endowed with 215k SNP markers data was phenotyped under a favorable and two managed drought environments. Trait-specific SNP subsets (28k) were selected for each trait under each environment, using results of GWAS performed with the complete genotype dataset. Performances of single-environment and multi-environment genomic prediction models were compared using kernel regression based methods (GBLUP and RKHS) under two cross validation scenarios: availability (CV2) or not (CV1) of phenotypic data for the validation set, in one of the environments. Trait-specific marker selection strategy achieved predictive ability (PA) of genomic prediction up to 22% higher than markers selected on the bases of neutral linkage disequilibrium (LD). Tolerance to drought stress was up to 32% better predicted by multi-environment models (especially RKHS based models) under CV2 strategy. Under the less favorable CV1 strategy, the multi-environment models achieved similar PA than the single-environment predictions. We also showed that reasonable PA could be obtained with as few as 3,000 SNP markers, even in a population of low LD extent, provided marker selection is based on pairwise LD. The implications of these findings for breeding for drought tolerance are discussed. The most resource sparing option would be accurate phenotyping of the reference population in a favorable environment and under a managed drought, while the candidate population would be phenotyped only under one of those environments.

text: The Rab family of small GTPases regulate various aspects of cellular dynamics in eukaryotic cells. Membrane trafficking has emerged as central to the functions of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2), which is associated with inherited and sporadic forms of Parkinson’s disease (PD). Rabs act as both regulators of the catalytic activity and targets for serine/threonine phosphorylation by LRRK2. Rab32, Rab38 and Rab29 have been shown to regulate LRRK2 sub-cellular localization through direct interactions. Recently, Rab29 was shown to escort LRRK2 to the Golgi apparatus and activate the phosphorylation of Rab8 and Rab10. Rab32 is linked to multiple cellular functions including endosomal trafficking, mitochondrial dynamics, and melanosome biogenesis. A missense mutation in Rab32 has also recently been linked to PD. Here, we demonstrate that Rab32 directly interacts with sorting nexin 6 (SNX6). SNX6 is a transient subunit of the retromer, an endosome-Golgi retrieval complex whose Vps35 subunit is strongly associated with PD. We could further show that localization of cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptors, which are recycled to the trans-Golgi network (TGN) by the retromer, was affected by both Rab32 and SNX6. These data imply that Rab32 is linked to SNX6/retromer trafficking at the Golgi, and also suggests a possible connection between the retromer and Rab32 in the trafficking and biological functions of LRRK2.

text: A disturbance of glucose homeostasis leading to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is one of the severe side effects that may occur during a prolonged use of many drugs currently available on the market. In this manuscript we describe the most common cases of drug-induced T2DM, discuss available pharmacotherapies and propose new ones. Among various pharmacotherapies of T2DM, incretin therapies have recently focused attention due to the newly determined crystal structure of incretin hormone receptor GLP1R. Incretin hormone receptors: GLP1R and GIPR together with the glucagon receptor GCGR regulate food intake and insulin and glucose secretion. Our study showed that incretin hormone receptors, named also gut hormone receptors as they are expressed in the gastrointestinal tract, could potentially act as unintended targets (off-targets) for orally administrated drugs. Such off-target interactions, depending on their effect on the receptor (stimulation or inhibition), could be beneficial, like in the case of incretin mimetics, or unwanted if they cause, e.g., decreased insulin secretion. In this in silico study we examined which well-known pharmaceuticals could potentially interact with gut hormone receptors in the off-target way. We observed that drugs with the strongest binding affinity for gut hormone receptors were also reported in the medical information resources as the least disturbing the glucose homeostasis among all drugs in their class. We suggested that those strongly binding molecules could potentially stimulate GIPR and GLP1R and/or inhibit GCGR which could lead to increased insulin secretion and decreased hepatic glucose production. Such positive effect on the glucose homeostasis could compensate for other, adverse effects of pharmacotherapy which lead to drug-induced T2DM. In addition, we also described several top hits as potential substitutes of peptidic incretin mimetics which were discovered in the drug repositioning screen using gut hormone receptors structures against the ZINC15 compounds subset.

text: In everyday life, people often combine strategies to regulate their emotions. However, to date, most research has investigated emotion regulation strategies as if they occur independently from one another. The current study aims to better understand the sequential interplay between strategies by investigating how reappraisal and rumination interact to affect anger experience. After participants (N = 156) recalled a recent anger-provoking event, they were instructed to either a) reappraise the event twice, b) reappraise the event, and then ruminate about the event, c) ruminate about the event, and then reappraise the event, or d) ruminate twice about the event. The effects of the first strategy used replicated a large body of research: reappraisal was associated with a decrease in anger, but rumination was associated with no change in anger. There was a small interactive effect of the combination of the two strategies, such that those who ruminated and then reappraised showed a larger decrease in anger than those who reappraised and then ruminated. There were no other differences between groups. This suggests that the second strategy does have an effect over and beyond the first strategy, but this effect is small in size, highlighting the importance of the initial emotion regulation strategy used.

text: Voltage-sensing phosphatases (VSPs) are transmembrane proteins that couple changes in membrane potential to hydrolysis of inositol signaling lipids. VSPs catalyze the dephosphorylation of phosphatidylinositol phosphates (PIPs) that regulate diverse aspects of cell membrane physiology including cell division, growth and migration. VSPs are highly conserved among chordates, and their RNA transcripts have been detected in the adult and embryonic stages of frogs, fish, chickens, mice and humans. However, the subcellular localization and biological function of VSP remains unknown. Using reverse transcriptase-PCR (RT-PCR), we show that both Xenopus laevis VSPs (Xl-VSP1 and Xl-VSP2) mRNAs are expressed in early embryos, suggesting that both Xl-VSPs are involved in early tadpole development. To understand which embryonic tissues express Xl-VSP mRNA, we used in situ hybridization (ISH) and found Xl-VSP mRNA in both the brain and kidney of NF stage 32–36 embryos. By Western blot analysis with a VSP antibody, we show increasing levels of Xl-VSP protein in the developing embryo, and by immunohistochemistry (IHC), we demonstrate that Xl-VSP protein is specifically localized to the apical membrane of both embryonic and adult kidney tubules. We further characterized the catalytic activity of both Xl-VSP homologs and found that while Xl-VSP1 catalyzes 3- and 5-phosphate removal, Xl-VSP2 is a less efficient 3-phosphatase with different substrate specificity. Our results suggest that Xl-VSP1 and Xl-VSP2 serve different functional roles and that VSPs are an integral component of voltage-dependent PIP signaling pathways during vertebrate kidney tubule development and function.

The Associated Press (AP) and CNN reported about midday UTC that the death toll in the Sunday's accident on K2 has risen to eleven.

Two Dutch climbers have been rescued by helicopter, the AP also said. CNN reports that two of the people killed were climbing up the mountain in an attempt to assist others.

AP says that about two dozen climbers began the accent of K2, the world's second-highest mountain, Friday after the weather had cleared. Climbers are listed as from the Netherlands, South Korea, Italy, Norway, France, Nepal, Serbia, Pakistan and Ireland.

Trouble began on Sunday when several climbers decided to turn back citing rope placement problems. CNN reports the group was climbing in two teams and both were descending from near the summit when an a large chuck of ice fell sweeping three people off the mountain.

Wilco Van Rooijen, one of the two rescued Dutch climbers, spoke to AP via phone. He blames poor planning in addition to the avalanche.

He told AP that a low-cloud bank caused whiteout on the mountain, but he chose to begin his decent from the area near the summit.

One stranded climber, Marco Confortola, an Italian who spoke with his brother by phone, described the events as hellish.

A helicopter rescue for Confortola had to be delayed due to poor weather. He told his brother that he was able to walk down to the base camp.

CNN reports that this is the deadliest accident on K2 since records were kept in 1939. 66 people — not counting those in the latest incident — have died on the mountain since then.

About 90 law enforcement officers from multiple agencies broke up what they said was a rave party on public and private property in the Diamond Fork area of Spanish Fork canyon, an hour outside of Salt Lake City, Utah, at about 11:30 p.m. Saturday (5:30 Sunday UTC).

According to the county, the Sheriff's Office had been investigating similar parties since the beginning of the season. In a press release from the Sheriff's Office in Utah County, the department states that previous allegations of sexual abuse at other raves, as well as various firearm and theft violations, were reasons for the investigation. The release continues on to state that the proper permit was not obtained before the event started. The promoters deny this allegation and insist that all permits were legally obtained before the event.

The police have publicly stated that only a permit from the health department was obtained, and that a Utah mass gathering permit was needed. The promoters have stated that they had the required permit, and have given a permit number (# 2005-11). Jay Stone, who handles mass gathering permits for the Utah County Health Department’s Bureau of Environmental Health Services, has confirmed that the permit was applied for and granted for the party. Officials also claim that the party had spilled over onto public land, and that more than 60 arrests were made in total - for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, underage drinking, drug possession and distribution, resisting arrest, assault on a police officer, disorderly conduct, and one instance of a weapons offense, a pistol which was found in the home of the private property owners. Among the confiscated items and drugs found were cocaine, ecstasy, marijuana, mushrooms, alcohol, and drug paraphernalia. Some of the drugs may include those confiscated from attendees by private security guards - who were also arrested.

Other event-goers felt that the use of force in the shutdown was excessive - numerous eyewitness accounts by concertgoers describe people being beaten, tasered, or attacked with dogs. An email from Sheriff Jim Tracy stated that dogs and tasers were present at the raid, however, he also states that the tasers were not used on anyone, and that no dogs were deployed against concertgoers.

Utah County sheriff's Sergeant Darren Gilbert also alleged that a 17-year-old girl was found overdosed on ecstasy, and was treated and released to her parents. According to an advertisement for the event, an attorney was present at the party. The local sheriff is scheduled to appear on Utah TV.

The death of a candidate for the Bundestag could delay the final outcome of the German federal election by several weeks.

The 43-year old Kerstin Lorenz, of the far right NPD, suffered a stroke during a campaign appearance on Monday and slid into a coma. She died on Wednesday in the hospital.

The NPD must now nominate a new candidate for the constituency of Dresden I and election officials have to reprint hundreds of thousands of ballot papers. Also, the vote of anyone who already sent in their absentee ballot will be declared invalid, and these voters need new ballots as well. The leading election official for the state of Saxonia, Irene Schneider-Böttcher, said it would be impossible to achieve all that was required within the time remaining before election day, September 18th. She ordered a by-election for the 2nd of October.

If the election results are extremely close, the outstanding Dresden I by-election result could potentially change the final outcome, which would leave Germany in uncertainty. While Dresden I is only one out of 299 constituencies, it could ultimately decide who will govern the country for the next few years.

The projected majority of the opposition parties FDP and CDU, which headed the polls for months, is shrinking with current government parties Greens and SPD, along with the Party of the Left, getting closer by the day.

Some constitutional lawyers have also raised concerns if it would be legal to announce any results at all on September 18th. They argue that in the case of a close result, the voters in Dresden would realize that they will be the one to decide the election, which could shift their votes. And on the other side, if the race is already over, they might decide to stay at home.

A blizzard hit Colorado and the plains dumping more than two feet of snow in Denver, rising to five feet in some areas north of Denver. Over 2500 flights stand canceled as |Denver International Airport, the fifth-busiest airport in the US, shut down on Wednesday. The airport is not expected to open until noon of Friday. Thousands of travelers have been stranded during the busy Christmas season.

Snow started to fall in Denver at dawn on Wednesday, and did not let up until Thursday afternoon. Sustained winds blowing at 20 miles per hour and gusts up to 50 mph created snow drifts reaching up to 5 feet in some places in Denver, especially in the northern suburbs. Long stretches of I-70, I-25, and I-76 were closed as it was impossible to plow through the blizzard.

The weather system led to school shutdowns in New Mexico because of the heavy snow and freezing rain, before moving across Colorado, which was the worst hit. Some mountain regions received up to 4 feet of snow, not counting the drifts. The system slowly moved northeastward and dumped fairly large amounts of snow in southeastern Wyoming, the Dakotas, and Kansas.

The World Health Organisation (WHO), in a statement issued Tuesday, urged scientists to destroy samples of a deadly flu virus that could potentially cause a global pandemic.

Shipments of the influenza virus sent to Mexico and Lebanon are unaccounted for. The U.N. health organization said 10 countries receiving samples already destroyed them, while 5 more countries are in the process of doing so.

The virus, A/H2N2, was detected by a Canadian lab which contacted the Public Health Agency of Canada, who in turn warned the WHO and other national health agencies on March 26.

Meridian Bioscience sent routine testing kits infected with the virus to almost 5,000 laboratories, of which 3747 in 18 countries have so far been identified as having the virus, most of them in North America.

The virus is a variant of the H2N2 virus which caused the 1957 Asian Flu Pandemic, but which was displaced by the H3N2 variant. People born after 1959 are unlikely to be immune to the virus.
